paragraphs.text: DSH plugin: detect, launch and verify Minecraft mod builds from the session header.
# minecraft-dev-starter
**Run and verify Minecraft mod builds from the DeepSeek Harness session header.**
English | 简体中文
The plugin detects Minecraft mod and plugin projects in the current workspace, offers run-target sel
ection plus start/stop controls in the session header, and streams launch logs into a sidebar tab.
The panel serves people, the tools serve the model, and both share one run state and one lock: a pro
ject has at most one instance, whoever started it, and neither side kills the other's process.
Run targets have two lifecycles. `runClient` / `runServer` are daemons that keep running until the w
indow is closed; `runData` / `runGameTestServer` finish and produce a pass or fail verdict. That is
what lets the model close its own "change code → run it → read the verdict" loop instead of asking a
human to judge a game window.
## Features
- **Project detection**: Fabric, Forge, NeoForge, Architectury, Paper and Spigot, from Minecraft 1.7
.10 to 26.x. Single-module, multi-module and composite builds are supported, including repositories

that declare their loader only in a submodule.
- **Run targets**: extracted from the Gradle build, s
plit into `daemon` and `oneshot`. Targets inferred by loader convention are marked unverified, and r

emain selectable and launchable.
- **Managed launches**: tasks are started through the Gradle wrappe
r. Daemons become "running" when their readiness markers appear in the log, not merely when the proc
ess is alive; one-shot tasks report success, failure, being stopped, or failing to start as distinct

outcomes. Stopping kills Gradle and its whole process tree.
- **JDK selection**: the required JDK m
ajor is inferred from the Minecraft version and `toolchain`. The panel lists the JDKs found on this
machine and can also register a JDK root directory you type in. Choices stay local (`~/.dsh/mc-dev-s
tarter/jdk.json`), never in `gradle.properties`, and are passed to Gradle as `-Dorg.gradle.java.home
` plus `JAVA_HOME`, so what the panel shows is what actually runs. Automatic selection only takes ov

er when the major version matches exactly and the wrapper's Gradle can run it.
- **Declared dependen
cies**: `dependencies { }` blocks, `gradle/libs.versions.toml` and the metadata `depends` are parsed
and shown with configuration, coordinate and `file:line`, so you can confirm that a dependency was
really added. Only declarations are shown — resolved transitive graphs require running Gradle. When
IntelliJ has synced the project, each declaration is also compared with the version from the IDE's l

ibrary table (no Gradle run); "actual x.y.z" is informational, not an error.
[该节后续省略]
## Compatibility
| Platform | Versions | Notes |

| Fabric | 1.14 – 26.x | `runClient` and friends from loom |
| Forge | 1.7.10 / 1.12.2 / 1.16.5 / 1.

20.1 | including legacyforge |
| NeoForge | 1.20.1 – 26.x | moddev plugin |
| Architectury | 1.16 –

26.x | targets split per submodule |
| Paper / Spigot | 1.7.10 – 26.x | server plugin projects |
The JDK level is inferred from the Minecraft version: 1.7.10 and 1.12.2 need Java 8, 1.18 to 1.20.4
need Java 17, 1.20.5 and above need Java 21, 26.x needs Java 25. The requirement is compared against
installed JDKs and mismatches are surfaced in the panel.
Multi-module builds are supported: each submodule is listed as its own project, its run targets carr
y the Gradle module prefix (`:modules/core:runClient`) and they launch from the aggregator root, whe
re the wrapper lives. When IntelliJ's `.idea` directory is present, its Gradle module list, minecraf
t facet platform, project JDK and run configurations are read as a **fallback** source — build scrip
ts stay authoritative and are never overridden.
Verified against **dsh 0.2.1-rc.4** (DSH NEXT 2.0.21-next) on Windows 11. Host-side changes are reco
rded in CHANGELOG; raising the supported range is treated as a breaking change.
## Security
Reporting channel, supported versions and the full threat model: SECURITY.md.
- **What it executes.** Launching a target runs the project's own Gradle wrapper (`gradlew.bat` / `g
radlew`) in the project directory, with the environment of the DSH host. That means the workspace's
build script runs with your user permissions — the same trust you extend by invoking `gradle` yourse

lf. Only targets discovered inside the workspace are offered.
- **What it touches.** Run state and l
ogs are written under `~/.dsh/mc-dev-starter` (per profile); the JDK choice lives in `jdk.json` next

to it. Nothing is written into the project beyond what Gradle itself writes.
- **What it sends.** N
othing leaves the machine. The `/mcdev/api` routes are served by the local DSH web server behind its

own authentication, and the client bundle posts diagnostics only to those routes.
- **Subprocesses.
** At most one target per project; stopping kills the whole process tree (Windows `taskkill /T`, POS
IX process group) so no orphan `java` process survives. No implicit `clean`, build directories are n

ever deleted.
- **Package contents.** No dependencies are declared, and no install or post-install s
cript runs on your machine — `prepack` only executes in the publisher's workspace.
Two advisories shown on the npm page are inherited from the host runtime, not from this package:
- `zod` (GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5) arrives via `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` → `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm`. This pa

ckage declares no dependencies and cannot pin it.
- "Uses eval" is a false positive on a string lite
ral in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-ptc-runtime`'s reserved-word table; `eval` does not appear in this reposito
ry or in the built bundle.
## Known limitations

- Native sidebar tab types have no icon field; icons only appear on `dsh-better-sidebar` tabs.
- An
aggregator root is not listed once its submodules are: if the root carries its own run targets, they

are not offered.
- `.idea` is a fallback source only. A module that is neither in `settings.gradle`
nor in the IDE module list is not discovered, and the facet platform never overrides a judged loade

r.
- One-shot verdicts combine the exit code with log markers: a non-zero exit is always a failure,
and a zero exit is still a failure when test-failure markers appear (for example `N required tests f
ailed`), so a runner that swallows a failure does not look like a pass. When neither is available th

e verdict is unknown.
- The first build on Windows downloads Gradle and the project's dependencies,
which can take several minutes; later builds reuse the Gradle daemon.
